title: A release claims a milestone number that doesn't exist
author: retrya
description: Reads a GitHub release's own body for every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (the shared seam_engine.milestone_claims grammar) and checks whether the named milestone exists at all. release-claims-open-milestone's own docstring named this exact seam and left it open on purpose: a claimed milestone number that names no real milestone at all was excluded there as belonging to 'dangling-issue-reference's own seam (over issues/PRs), not this one's (over milestones).' A live recheck (task 870) found that deferral had never actually been built for the milestone number space: release-note-dangling-reference reads a release body for a bare #N, but strictly against the shared issue/PR number sequence, and never opens ListMilestones. This recipe is that seam, on the fourth of the five sources task 870 named and left open (release, tweet remained after mention/870, milestone/871, and readme/872 closed the first three) -- the release-sourced sibling of commit-claims-dangling-milestone, issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone, linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, mention-claims-dangling-milestone, milestone-claims-dangling-milestone, and readme-claims-dangling-milestone. Not whether a real milestone's claim is TRUE (release-claims-open-milestone's own remit), but whether the number the claim names resolves to anything real.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.8, not age-gated -- mirrors commit-claims-dangling-milestone's/issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone's/linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/mention-claims-dangling-milestone's/milestone-claims-dangling-milestone's/readme-claims-dangling-milestone's own reasoning rather than release-claims-open-milestone's 24-hour publish-age grace bar: that recipe age-gates because an OPEN milestone could close at any moment, so a fresh claim about it might just be a race the milestone tracker hasn't caught up to yet -- but a milestone number that does not exist right now will not spontaneously start existing later, so no grace period would mean anything here. A claimed milestone number that DOES resolve to a real milestone is excluded at confidence 0.0 regardless of whether that milestone is open or closed -- whether the claim is true is release-claims-open-milestone's own seam, not this one's. A release with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all produces no surfaced candidate -- there is no claim to have broken -- and this is named as an exclusion, not returned silently.
